description.en: The aim of the experiment is to study and measure the power consumed by a three-phase resistive load using the two-wattmeter method.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.

The **CHECK** button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.

**Note:** If a wire is connected incorrectly, click the corresponding label number to remove the connection.
The **AUTO CONNECT** button makes all the connections automatically.
The **ADD** button adds the readings to the observation table.
The **RESET** button refreshes the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The **PRINT** button allows you to print the simulation.

The MCB acts as the main power switch for the experiment. It also protects the circuit by automatically disconnecting the power supply in case of an overload or short circuit. When turned ON, it supplies electrical power to the circuit.

**Rating:** 16A, 3P, 415V AC, 50 Hz

This voltmeter is used to measure the line voltage (Vₗ). It is connected between the R and Y Phases of the three-phase supply to measure the voltage supplied to the load.

**Rating:** 0 - 600 V

This ammeter is used to measure the load current (Iₗ) flowing through the load. It is connected in series with the phase of the circuit.

**Rating:** 0 - 10 A

The two wattmeters are used to measure the total active power consumed by the three-phase balanced load. Its current coil is connected in series with the R and B phases, while its pressure coil is connected to the Y-phase. The total active power is given by the algebraic sum of the two wattmeter readings (P = W₁ + W₂).

**Rating:** 0 - 600W
The three load branches have left terminals 16, 18, 20 and right terminals 17, 19, 21. Lamps are off until the verified MCB is on. Star glows dimly; Delta glows brightly.
This table records the measured line voltage (Vₗ), line current (Iₗ), and Power (W₁ and W₂) for Star and Delta Load.
This section displays an equation used to calculate the theoretical three-phase active power for Star and Delta connection Load.

This is the theoretical verification panel. For verification, you have to calculate power for both connections. Enter the required values and compare the calculated power with the measured power to verify them.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table and theoretical verification, generate the report. The report will include the time taken to complete the simulation, no. of attempts, the apparatus used, recorded readings, the user-calculated result, and the conclusion.
